aboutH2: Medicentres Occupational Health Calgary: Workplace Drug and Alcohol Testing in Southeast Calgary
intro: Wellpoint’s team of Occupational Health professionals have significant experience with issues of substance abuse, drug and alcohol policy, procedure and testing protocols, as well as Employee Assistance Program interaction.

The clinic now runs as the Calgary location of Medicentres Occupational Health Services, and Google lists it as Wellpoint (Medicentres) Occupational Health. Its addiction-related work is for employers: drug and alcohol testing, reasonable-suspicion training for supervisors and an online awareness course for staff. It does not offer detox, counselling or any treatment program, so if you are looking for help with your own drinking or drug use, start with the Calgary treatment listings linked further down this page.

pillars.title: A Walk-In and Occupational Health Clinic Off Barlow Trail SE
pillars.body: The clinic is in unit 202 of a low commercial building at the corner of 61 Avenue SE and Barlow Trail SE, in the Foothills industrial area of southeast Calgary. Medicentres says it sits toward the back of the lot behind the Centex gas station, with parking on site and a transit connection. The same space works as Foothills Medicentres, a family walk-in clinic open Monday to Friday from 8:30am to 5pm, so the waiting room is shared with people there for family care or a driver's medical.

pillars.kicker: What it does and does not do
pillars.title: Testing for Employers: Not a Rehab
pillars.body: Medicentres describes drug and alcohol testing as a core part of its occupational health work. It builds testing programs around each employer, follows the panel set by the Canadian Model for Providing a Safe Workplace and the U.S. DOT program, and runs DOT FMCSA program management for carriers. Testing happens at the clinic, at the worksite or through mobile visits, and employer clients can call in emergency tests at any hour. The clinic has no beds and offers no counselling or treatment. A positive test usually leads back to the employer's own policy, its employee assistance program or a referral to treatment elsewhere, such as the publicly funded services run by Recovery Alberta.

pillars.title: Occupational Health Nurses, Physicians and a Substance Abuse Professional
pillars.body: Medicentres says its occupational health nurses and physicians do the medical exams and consult with employers on legislation and fitness for work. Supervisor training on spotting impairment and handling reasonable-suspicion cases is led by a certified Substance Abuse Professional (SAP) with experience in disability management and return-to-duty processes. Staff also run an online course that teaches employees about substance use, how it can progress and why suspected impairment should be reported. The clinic does not publish the names of its occupational health staff.

overviewH2: Medicentres Occupational Health Calgary: Clinic Overview
overview: Medicentres Occupational Health Services has four locations in Western Canada, in Saskatoon, Regina, Calgary and Edmonton, plus a network of more than 200 partner clinics across the country. This southeast Calgary clinic is the Calgary site. Its occupational health work covers pre-placement and periodic medicals, hearing tests and hearing conservation, lung function testing and respirator clearance, workplace immunization, wellness screening and drug and alcohol testing.
serviceCaption: 11 services · as described by Medicentres for its occupational health clinics and this location
afterOverview: For an injured worker, the clinic is also an Occupational Injury Service (OIS) site under WCB Alberta. Medicentres says injured workers are usually seen within 30 minutes, reports go to WCB the same day, and each worker gets a plan for modified duties and a return to work. Family care at the Foothills clinic is billed to the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan, so bring your Alberta Health Care card and photo ID.

location.heading: Medicentres Occupational Health Calgary in Calgary, Alberta
location.intro: The clinic is at 61 Avenue SE and Barlow Trail SE, in the Foothills industrial area of southeast Calgary, about 15 to 20 minutes from downtown by Deerfoot Trail or Glenmore Trail. Chestermere is about 20 minutes away, Airdrie and Okotoks are each around 35 minutes, and Red Deer is close to an hour and 45 minutes up Highway 2.

faqIntro: Answers come from Medicentres' own pages and the clinic's Google listing. Looking for treatment rather than testing? Call us, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Medicentres Occupational Health Calgary an addiction treatment centre?
faqs.a: No. It is an occupational health and walk-in medical clinic that does drug and alcohol testing for employers. There is no detox, counselling or residential program. For treatment in Calgary, look at the rehab and outpatient listings on our Calgary page or contact Recovery Alberta, which runs the province's publicly funded addiction services.

faqs.q: What drug and alcohol services does the clinic offer?
faqs.a: It offers workplace drug and alcohol testing at the clinic, at worksites and through mobile visits, with 24/7 emergency testing for employer clients. Medicentres also manages DOT FMCSA testing programs, trains supervisors on reasonable suspicion and runs an online drug and alcohol awareness course for employees.

faqs.q: Can I get emergency or post-incident testing after hours?
faqs.a: Yes, for employers who are clients. Medicentres Occupational Health Services says it provides 24/7 emergency drug and alcohol testing as well as scheduled on-site testing. Employers book through the occupational health line at 1-877-374-9079 or ccbookings@medicentres.com.

faqs.q: Where is the clinic and how do I get there?
faqs.a: It is at 3716 61 Ave SE, unit 202, at the corner of 61 Avenue SE and Barlow Trail SE in southeast Calgary. Medicentres says the clinic is toward the back of the parking lot from the Centex gas station, and it can be reached by car or transit with parking on site. Downtown Calgary is about 15 to 20 minutes away by car.

The clinic is open Monday to Friday from 8:30am to 5pm and closed on weekends. Medicentres notes that hours can change and posts current hours and wait times on its online wait timer. Emergency drug and alcohol testing for employer clients runs around the clock.

faqs.q: Who runs the clinic now? Is it still WellPoint?
faqs.a: Medicentres runs it as the Calgary location of Medicentres Occupational Health Services, and Medavie bought Medicentres Canada in April 2025. Google still lists the clinic as Wellpoint (Medicentres) Occupational Health, and older photos show WellPoint signs at this address. The WellPoint website now says WellPoint is part of Kii Health.

faqs.q: Is it covered by Alberta Health Care?
faqs.a: Family and walk-in visits are billed to the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan, so bring your health card and photo ID. Workplace testing and medicals are arranged with employers, and Medicentres does not publish prices for them. Driver's medicals are an uninsured service.

faqs.q: What is the OIS program at this clinic?
faqs.a: OIS is a WCB Alberta program that gives workers injured on the job quick access to a physician. Medicentres says OIS patients are usually seen within 30 minutes, reports go to WCB the same day, and each worker gets a plan for modified duties and a return to work. The employer must be enrolled in the OIS program.

faqs.q: Can the clinic help me if I am worried about my own drinking or drug use?
faqs.a: Not with treatment. The clinic tests and trains on behalf of employers. If your workplace has an employee assistance program, it is a confidential place to start, and Recovery Alberta, private centres and outpatient programs in Calgary can help with assessment and treatment.
